subject.title: fix(acpx): keep leaked non-openai model out of the Codex ACP thinking slot

question: Should OpenClaw accept modelExplicit and appliedModel as the ACP runtime boundary for distinguishing inherited defaults from explicit Codex ACP model selections?
rationale: The patch appears correct, but the API shape and fallback-versus-fail-closed behavior affect compatibility, provider/model routing, and plugin runtime contracts.

options.title: Accept provenance contract
options.body: Land with modelExplicit and appliedModel as the intended additive boundary because it fixes both spawn and first-turn replay without Codex-specific policy in core persistence.

options.title: Narrow the runtime API
options.body: Ask for a smaller Codex-only contract if maintainers do not want generic ACP runtime fields for model provenance and effective model reporting.

options.title: Pause this branch
options.body: Keep the PR open but paused if fallback behavior for inherited unsupported defaults needs a broader product/API decision first.

recommendation.title: Accept provenance contract
recommendation.body: Land with modelExplicit and appliedModel as the intended additive boundary because it fixes both spawn and first-turn replay without Codex-specific policy in core persistence.
